source_text:
Ἡ προσευχὴ ὑμῶν ἀπῆλθεν ἐπὶ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τὴν ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ τῆς Συρίας, ὅθεν δεδεμένος θεοπρεπεστάτοις δεσμοῖς πάντας ἀσπάζομαι, οὐκ ὢν ἄξιος ἐκεῖθεν εἶναι, ἔσχατος αὐτῶν ὤν: κατὰ θέλημα δὲ κατηξιώθην, οὐκ ἐκ συνειδότος ἀλλ’ ἐκ χάριτος θεοῦ: ἣν εὔχομαι τελείαν μοι δοθῆναι, ἵνα ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ ὑμῶν θεοῦ ἐπιτύχω.
ἵνα οὖν ὑμῶν τέλειον γένηται τὸ ἔργον καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς καὶ ἐν οὐρανῷ, πρέπει εἰς τιμὴν θεοῦ χειροτονῆσαι τὴν ἐκκλησίαν ὑμῶν θεοπρεσβεύτην, εἰς τὸ γενόμενον ἐν Συρίᾳ συγχαρῆναι αὐτοῖς, ὅτι εἰρηνεύουσιν καὶ ἀπέλαβον τὸ ἴδιον μέγεθος καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη αὐτοῖς τὸ ἴδιον σωματεῖον.
ἐφάνη μοι οὖν θεοῦ ἄξιον πρᾶγμα, πέμψαι τινὰ τῶν ὑμετέρων μετ’ ἐπιστολῆς, ἵνα συνδοξάσῃ τὴν κατὰ θεὸν αὐτοῖς γενομένην εὐδίαν, καὶ ὅτι λιμένος ἤδη ἐτύγχανον τῇ προσευχῇ ὑμῶν. τέλειοι ὄντες τέλεια καὶ φρονεῖτε. θέλουσιν γὰρ ὑμῖν εὖ πράσσειν θεὸς ἕτοιμος εἰς τὸ παρέχειν.
thought_title: Send a delegate to Antioch to rejoice with the restored church
orientation: Ignatius, writing to the Smyrnaeans, has just praised them for receiving his companions and now asks them to send a representative to the church in Antioch, which has regained peace.
pass_a_gloss: Your prayer went up to the church in Antioch of Syria, from where, bound with bonds most befitting God, I greet all, not being worthy to be from there, being the last of them: but according to the will I was counted worthy, not from conscience but from the grace of God: which I pray may be given to me perfect, so that in your prayer I may attain God. So that therefore your work may become perfect both on earth and in heaven, it is fitting for the honor of God to ordain a godly elder for your church, to rejoice together with them over what has happened in Syria, because they are at peace and received back their own greatness and their own body was restored to them. It seemed to me therefore a thing worthy of God, to send one of your own with a letter, so that he may join in glorifying the calm that came to them from God, and because they already reached harbor by your prayer. Being perfect, think perfect things. For God is ready to grant you to fare well.

choices.why: Keeps the superlative force and the compound adjective's sense of fitting God, without flattening to 'divine'
Renders the compound literally: one sent on an embassy for God, preserving the diplomatic sense
Keeps the corporate-body metaphor for the church, matching the literal sense of σωματεῖον as an organized body
Preserves the nautical metaphor of arriving at a safe harbor, which the literal verb τυγχάνω with genitive conveys
Keeps the wordplay of τέλειοι/τέλεια and the imperative force of φρονεῖτε
rejected: Since you are perfect, be perfect-minded

pass_b_english: Your prayer reached the church in Antioch of Syria. From there I greet you all, bound as I am in chains most worthy of God. I am not worthy to come from that place, for I am the least of them. Yet by God's will I was counted worthy, not because of my own conscience but by the grace of God. I pray that this grace may be given to me in full, so that through your prayer I may attain God.

So that your work may be complete both on earth and in heaven, it is fitting for the honor of God that your church appoint a godly ambassador. He should go to Syria and rejoice with the church there, because they are at peace, have received back their own greatness, and their own body has been restored to them.

It seemed to me, then, a thing worthy of God to send one of your own with a letter, so that he might join in glorifying the calm that has come to them from God, and because they have already reached harbor through your prayer. Since you are perfect, think perfect things. For God is ready to grant you well-being.

problems.why: Greek says to ordain a godly elder/bishop for the church; English renders it as sending a delegate to God, changing who is appointed and to whom.
problems.fix: ordain a godly elder (bishop) for your church

edits.old: that your church appoint a delegate to God, to go to Syria and rejoice with them
edits.new: that your church ordain a godly elder for itself, to go to Syria and rejoice with them

fixed: The agency problem was real: the English changed who is appointed and to whom. Fixed by rendering χειροτονῆσαι as 'ordain' and θεοπρεσβεύτην as 'a godly elder for itself'.

problems.quote: it is fitting for the honor of God that your church ordain a godly elder for itself, to go to Syria and rejoice with them that they are at peace, have received back their own greatness, and their own body has been restored to them.
problems.why: 'their own greatness' and 'their own body' refer to church of Antioch but antecedent distant; 'body' as church body is metaphorical and abrupt.
problems.fix: Clarify referent: 'the church at Antioch has received back its former greatness, and its own body [the full congregation] has been restored.'

edits.old: have received back their own greatness, and their own body has been restored to them.
edits.new: have received back their own greatness, and their own body has been restored to them—the church at Antioch.

fixed: Clarified the referent of 'their own greatness' and 'their own body' by adding '—the church at Antioch' at the end of the clause, since the source's 'αὐτοῖς' refers to the church in Antioch, and the antecedent is distant.

last_rejected.why: Brief maps πρεσβυτέριον to 'council of elders'; θεοπρεσβεύτην means a venerable person, not an elder to be ordained.
last_rejected.ruling: θεοπρεσβεύτην = godly elder, not council; glossary entry appropriate.

last_rejected.why: Here means 'appoint/choose' a delegate, not ecclesiastical ordination.
last_rejected.ruling: χειροτονῆσαι means to ordain/appoint by laying on of hands; 'ordain' acceptable.

last_rejected.why: χειροτονῆσαι takes double accusative: 'appoint your church as delegate', not 'your church ordain for itself.'
last_rejected.ruling: Double accusative shows appointing an elder for the church; translation conveys that.
συνειδότος here means 'conscience'; 'not from conscience but from grace' is standard and correct.

last_rejected.quote: glorifying the calm that has come to them from God
last_rejected.fix: glorifying the good that has come to them from God
last_rejected.ruling: εὐδία means 'fair weather, calm, peace'; 'calm' fits the context of peace restored in Syria.

polish.changed: Clarified that the ambassador is appointed by the church, made the antecedent of 'their own greatness' and 'their own body' explicit as the church in Antioch, and smoothed sentence flow for reading aloud.

notes.quote: it is fitting for the honor of God that your church ordain a godly elder for itself, to go to Syria and rejoice with them that they are at peace, have received back their own greatness, and their own body has been restored to them.
notes.why: 'their own greatness' and 'their own body' refer to church of Antioch but antecedent distant; 'body' as church body is metaphorical and abrupt.
notes.fix: Clarify referent: 'the church at Antioch has received back its former greatness, and its own body [the full congregation] has been restored.'

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker and referents, smoothed sentence order, and made the flow more natural for reading aloud while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.quote: their own body has been restored to them
notes.why: Unclear what 'body' means—the church body, the physical body of members, or a metaphor.
notes.fix: Clarify that 'body' means the church community restored to unity.
